title: Eden as the Israel team's operational territory
statement: Eden is read, per the canon, as the operational territory of the Israel team of Elohim creators — the site of the biological-synthesis work that produced the first humans, of the disclosure episode, and of the expulsion that follows it; the corpus's placement of that territory on the antediluvian supercontinent is a geographical inference riding on the canonical reading and labelled as such.

includes: The canonical layer: Eden as the creation team's laboratory territory and garden, the scientific books of the disclosure episode, and the expulsion — the events the canon narrates in its Genesis reading
The conflict placement: the disclosure and expulsion as the opening episode of the conflict recorded as woh-claim-0008
The geographical layer, inferred and labelled: the territory placed on the antediluvian supercontinent of the corpus's reconstruction, going beyond what the canon states
excludes: Identification of Eden with any modern location or archaeological site
The rivers geography of Genesis 2 as a solvable map; the corpus does not perform that identification
Any claim that the Genesis redactor understood the laboratory reading
The expulsion's aftermath, which belongs to woh-claim-0008's arc

source_references.locator: Chapter 2 (Eden, the scientific books, the serpent faction and its exile — the sequence the Archdeacon Explainer locates at paragraphs 28-39)
GEN-WOH-2:8-17 (the garden and the trees); 3:1-24 (the disclosure narrative and the expulsion)
The critical treatment of the garden narrative and its ancient Near Eastern background

alternatives.statement: The garden narrative is a wisdom-and-mortality aetiology within ancient Near Eastern garden-of-god tradition; no site or team stands behind it.
The rivers geography points to a literary Mesopotamian setting, which explains the narrative's furniture without any operational territory.
The supercontinent placement stacks a corpus reconstruction on a canonical reading; the geographical layer should be retired even if the canonical layer stands.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0008 is revised or retired.
Source-language review of GEN-WOH-2-3 changes the observations the reading relies on.
The supercontinent reconstruction is revised, requiring the geographical layer to move with it or detach.
Public prose begins identifying Eden with a modern location, which this record excludes.
